life_summary: Joseph Smith Jr. was born December 23, 1805, in Sharon, Vermont, during a period of intense religious ferment known as the Second Great Awakening. His family struggled financially throughout his youth, moving frequently in search of economic opportunity. Smith received limited formal education but displayed early inclination toward spiritual matters and folk traditions. In 1823, he claimed to have received a vision of an angel named Moroni, beginning a series of revelatory experiences that would define his life. He grew to manhood in western New York, where he worked as a farm laborer and treasure seeker before his religious calling transformed him into one of America's most influential religious founders.
church_summary: Smith founded the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in 1830 at age twenty-four, publishing the Book of Mormon and claiming authority as prophet and president of the Church. He established settlements in Ohio, Missouri, and Illinois, serving as prophet, presiding officer, and theological innovator throughout his ministry. He introduced controversial doctrines including polygamy, baptism for the dead, and temple endowment ceremonies. Smith was killed June 27, 1844, in Carthage, Illinois, by a mob that stormed the jail, making him the first U.S. presidential candidate to be assassinated. His death propelled the movement toward westward expansion under successor leadership.
